title.text: Layered course system for agent development

principles.0.text: This file is the single source of truth for course categories, lesson numbers, prerequisites, and planning status. The web pages, the API, and the course docs are all generated from it.

principles.1.text: Lessons are identified by a stable slug. When a lesson is renamed, its old slug is registered as an alias. Displayed lesson numbers are computed from the order of registration in the catalog, so inserting a new lesson does not change any ID. "available" means the platform has the experiments, not that the learner has mastered the lesson. "planned" lessons only show the plan and cannot be run yet.

principles.2.text: Each lesson moves through goals, principles, code reading, prediction, experiments, trace comparison, and self-check. The planned experiments listed below are requirements for later production; registering a lesson does not mean its material and code are finished.

principles.3.text: Prerequisites follow knowledge dependencies. RAG does not require persistent memory first, LangChain does not require finishing Agentic RAG first, and standalone evaluation can start after the task acceptance lesson.

principles.4.text: Starting from {{lesson:task-contract}}, build a minimal acceptance case, and keep success and edge cases through every stage. {{lesson:evaluation-sets}} then studies independent verification, held-out sets, and regression in one place.

principles.5.text: Use a provider-independent, unified model interface, with Bailian as the configuration tested so far. Other services are supported through a mature SDK or an adapter layer, and the raw HTTP and the adapter-layer input and output are kept separately. Controlled-variable experiments fix the model and configuration for that run and are not tied to one long-term provider. Each new framework is installed as an optional dependency per lesson; check the official docs and pin the version when it is implemented.

principles.6.text: From the document-loading lesson on, external text is treated as untrusted. The full permission and prompt injection experiments are done in {{lesson:prompt-injection}}. The program decides which tools may run; a prompt cannot replace permission control.

principles.7.text: Each stage adds capability to the same local study assistant while keeping small experiments that can run on their own. A stage's result is accepted by its citations, parameters, state, actual side effects, and terminal state.

principles.8.text: Course experiments use real models and real tools. Simulation is only for internal automated tests and is not the main learning path. Replay does not re-run tools or models. Model output, tool results, and state updates are recorded separately; provider-measured, estimated, and unknown metrics are clearly distinguished; and an animation is never presented as the model's internal thinking.

principles.9.text: Reference projects supply structure and engineering ideas; the course's descriptions and experiments are written from scratch. Having read a source, the source existing, historical tests, and a local reproduction are each stated separately, references are pinned to a fixed snapshot, and the course does not claim to have implemented a whole tutorial.

category.A.description.text: Start from a single model request and work up to real Python tool calls, and learn to read the model's decisions, execution results, and failure boundaries.

module.A0.description.text: One request, multi-turn history, and sampling variance: every later lesson builds on these three things.

module.A1.description.text: From call proposal to executing and returning the result, and then to data dependencies between tools.

module.A2.description.text: Use failure cases to pin down what validation, the allowlist, and stop conditions are responsible for.

category.B.description.text: Turn a requirement into a task that can be accepted, and constrain behavior with explicit input, output, and tool contracts.

module.B1.description.text: Define success criteria and tell structurally valid output apart from business-correct output.

module.B2.description.text: Compare the effect of prompts and tool descriptions with controlled variables.

category.C.description.text: Manage the next round of model input, application state, and cross-session memory, while keeping evidence and users isolated.

module.C1.description.text: Tell message history apart from the task state the program maintains.

module.C2.description.text: Within a limited budget, keep the goal, constraints, sources, and unfinished work.

module.C3.description.text: Manage where a memory comes from and how it is stored, retrieved, updated, and forgotten.

module.C4.description.text: How a stable prefix is reused, and how skill instructions enter the context only when needed.

category.R.description.text: From text actions to planning, reflection, and workflow patterns, compare the reliability and cost that each way of controlling the model brings.

module.R1.description.text: Text actions compared with native calls, and TODO planning.

module.R2.description.text: Revising the plan after a failure, and a bounded review loop.

module.R3.description.text: Chaining, routing, parallelization, orchestration, and review-and-revise.

category.D.description.text: Turn local documents into retrievable evidence, and build answers that cite their sources and recognize when the documents are not enough.

module.D1.description.text: Loading and chunking, then comparing keyword, vector, and hybrid retrieval.

module.D2.description.text: Validate citations, then study bounded Agentic RAG.

category.E.description.text: Use one task to understand what LangChain wraps, then use LangGraph to express state, branches, and long-running tasks.

module.E1.description.text: Map native models, tools, and result contracts onto it, and reuse mature components.

module.E2.description.text: Build a state graph you can explain, and decide the boundaries for dependencies, concurrency, and cancellation.

module.E3.description.text: Add a gate before execution, pause and resume later, and recover from a checkpoint.

category.K.description.text: Let an agent run commands and edit files in an isolated environment, with the platform doing the acceptance check independently.

module.K1.description.text: Sandboxed command execution and file edits that can be verified.

category.F.description.text: Judge and improve an agent's behavior with independent evaluation, real observation, and constraints on the execution side.

module.F1.description.text: Build a fixed question set and held-out cases, and tell apart finished, correct, and well-evidenced.

module.F2.description.text: Connect run events, latency, failure attribution, and the usage the provider actually reports.

module.F3.description.text: Control the effects of retries, idempotency, permissions, and untrusted text.

category.G.description.text: Understand how MCP connects tool services, and manage real protocol calls and the connection lifecycle.

module.G1.description.text: Reuse existing business tools to do service discovery and calls.

module.G2.description.text: Manage connections to several services, and compare how MCP and A2A divide the work.

category.H.description.text: Compare the benefits and costs of multiple agents, and deliver a local study assistant that has passed acceptance.

module.H1.title.text: Multi-agent division of work and coordination

module.H1.description.text: Design delegation, context isolation, result merging, and the overall budget.

module.H2.description.text: The boundaries of background execution, scheduled triggers, and goal loops.

module.H3.title.text: Local delivery and the capstone project

module.H3.description.text: Produce a complete application that can start, resume, and be evaluated.
